```{r}
#| label: load-packages-r
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(nanoparquet)
library(tidymodels)
library(scales)
library(ggridges)
library(ggrepel)

# The factor zoo of lectures 10 to 14
sample_start <- ymd("1973-01-01")
sample_end <- ymd("2023-12-31")
test_start <- ymd("2000-01-01")
n_folds <- 5
ridge_lambdas <- 10^seq(-7, -1, by = 0.25)
lasso_lambdas <- 10^seq(-6, -2.5, by = 0.25)
macro_names <- c("dp", "tbl", "tms", "dfy", "svar")
# Number of PCA and RP-PCA factors: up to 60, chosen by cross-validation as in
# lecture 12
max_factors <- 60
phi_rp <- 10
n_trees <- 100
forest_grid <- expand_grid(mtry = c(1, 3, 7), min_n = c(500, 2000))

months_per_year <- 12

# Test sample in labels, e.g. 2000–2023
test_years <- paste0(year(test_start), "–", year(sample_end))

# Numbers with a typographic minus sign: values already in percent on axes,
# shares in tables and text
percent_axis <- label_number(suffix = "%", style_negative = "minus")
percent_text <- function(x, accuracy) {
  percent(x, accuracy, style_negative = "minus")
}
number_text <- function(x, accuracy, ...) {
  number(x, accuracy, style_negative = "minus", ...)
}

# Private on eumel until the papers are public: the factor library paper, with
# the composite spread and the paths of OSAP and JKP, and Scheuch & Voigt
# (2026) on the construction premium
factor_library_paper <- "~/claude-home/paper-factor-library"
construction_paper <- "~/claude-home/apt-and-nse"

# Colours of the slides, used by the figures
ku_red <- "#901A1E"
jet <- "#3d3d3d"
grey <- "#666666"
light <- "#e6e3df"
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
)

source("lecture-slides/_live-poll.R")
scoreboard_survey <- "aef27-ex08-scoreboard"
```

```{r}
#| label: lectures-10-to-14-code
#| include: false
#| cache: true
#| cache.extra: !expr list(sample_start, sample_end, test_start, n_folds, ridge_lambdas, lasso_lambdas, macro_names, max_factors, phi_rp, n_trees, forest_grid)
# Every row of the scoreboard, with the code of lectures 10 to 14

# Lecture 10: the zoo, the sample split, the Sharpe ratio metric and the
# workflows. Months start on their first day, as in lectures 13 and 14
osap_url <- paste0(
  "https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenSourceAP/CrossSection/resolve/",
  "Data-Release-2026.10/Portfolios/Full%20Sets%20OP/PredictorLSretWide.parquet"
)
osap_file <- "data/osap_long_short_returns.parquet"
if (!file.exists(osap_file)) {
  download.file(osap_url, osap_file, mode = "wb")
}
anomalies <- read_parquet(osap_file) |>
  mutate(date = floor_date(date, "month")) |>
  filter(between(date, sample_start, sample_end)) |>
  select(date, where(\(x) !anyNA(x))) |>
  mutate(across(-date, \(x) x / 100), y = 1)
anomaly_names <- setdiff(names(anomalies), c("date", "y"))
sample_split <- make_splits(
  filter(anomalies, date < test_start),
  assessment = filter(anomalies, date >= test_start)
)
estimation_months <- training(sample_split)
test_months <- testing(sample_split)
x_estimation <- as.matrix(estimation_months[anomaly_names])

sharpe_ratio_vec <- function(truth, estimate, ...) {
  mean(estimate) / sd(estimate) * sqrt(months_per_year)
}
sharpe_ratio <- function(data, truth, estimate, ...) {
  numeric_metric_summarizer(
    "sharpe_ratio",
    sharpe_ratio_vec,
    data,
    !!enquo(truth),
    !!enquo(estimate)
  )
}
sharpe_ratio <- new_numeric_metric(sharpe_ratio, direction = "maximize")

plug_in_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_variables(outcomes = y, predictors = all_of(anomaly_names)) |>
  add_model(linear_reg(), formula = y ~ 0 + .)
plug_in_fit <- fit(plug_in_workflow, estimation_months)
ridge_model <- linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = 0) |>
  set_engine(
    "glmnet",
    intercept = FALSE,
    standardize = FALSE,
    path_values = ridge_lambdas,
    control = list(thresh = 1e-12)
  )
ridge_workflow <- update_model(plug_in_workflow, ridge_model)
lasso_model <- linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = 1) |>
  set_engine(
    "glmnet",
    intercept = FALSE,
    standardize = FALSE,
    path_values = lasso_lambdas,
    control = list(thresh = 1e-12)
  )
lasso_workflow <- update_model(plug_in_workflow, lasso_model)

# Lecture 11: the penalties chosen by cross-validation on k = 5 consecutive
# blocks of the estimation months
block_folds <- estimation_months |>
  mutate(block = ceiling(dense_rank(date) / (n_distinct(date) / n_folds))) |>
  group_vfold_cv(group = block, v = n_folds)
ridge_tuning <- tune_grid(
  ridge_workflow,
  block_folds,
  grid = tibble(penalty = ridge_lambdas),
  metrics = metric_set(sharpe_ratio)
)
ridge_fit <- ridge_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(select_best(ridge_tuning, metric = "sharpe_ratio")) |>
  fit(estimation_months)
lasso_tuning <- tune_grid(
  lasso_workflow,
  block_folds,
  grid = tibble(penalty = lasso_lambdas),
  metrics = metric_set(sharpe_ratio)
)
lasso_fit <- lasso_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(select_best(lasso_tuning, metric = "sharpe_ratio")) |>
  fit(estimation_months)
ridge_lambda <- select_best(ridge_tuning, metric = "sharpe_ratio")$penalty

pc_lasso_weights <- function(months, lambda) {
  x <- as.matrix(months[anomaly_names])
  components <- eigen(cov(x), symmetric = TRUE)$vectors
  lasso_fit <- lasso_model |>
    finalize_model(tibble(penalty = lambda)) |>
    fit_xy(as.data.frame(x %*% components), months$y)
  components %*% tidy(lasso_fit)$estimate[-1]
}
pc_lasso_cv <- map_dbl(lasso_lambdas, \(lambda) {
  map_dbl(block_folds$splits, \(split) {
    weights <- pc_lasso_weights(analysis(split), lambda)
    validation <- assessment(split)
    portfolio_returns <- as.matrix(validation[anomaly_names]) %*% weights
    sharpe_ratio_vec(validation$y, portfolio_returns[, 1])
  }) |>
    mean()
})
pc_lasso_lambda <- lasso_lambdas[which.max(pc_lasso_cv)]

# Lecture 12: PCA and RP-PCA, the number of factors chosen in the same folds
factor_weights <- function(months, k, phi = 0) {
  x <- as.matrix(months[anomaly_names])
  mu <- colMeans(x)
  vectors <- eigen(cov(x) + phi * tcrossprod(mu), symmetric = TRUE)$vectors
  loadings <- vectors[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE]
  factors <- x %*% loadings
  loadings %*% solve(cov(factors), colMeans(factors))
}
factor_cv <- expand_grid(phi = c(0, phi_rp), factors = seq_len(max_factors)) |>
  mutate(
    cv = map2_dbl(phi, factors, \(phi, k) {
      map_dbl(block_folds$splits, \(split) {
        weights <- factor_weights(analysis(split), k, phi)
        validation <- assessment(split)
        portfolio_returns <- as.matrix(validation[anomaly_names]) %*% weights
        sharpe_ratio_vec(validation$y, portfolio_returns[, 1])
      }) |>
        mean()
    })
  )
chosen_factors <- factor_cv |>
  group_by(phi) |>
  slice_max(cv) |>
  ungroup()
pca_factors <- chosen_factors$factors[chosen_factors$phi == 0]
rp_pca_factors <- chosen_factors$factors[chosen_factors$phi == phi_rp]

# The weights of the SDF portfolios on the anomalies
fitted_weights <- function(fit) {
  estimates <- tidy(fit)
  estimates$estimate[match(anomaly_names, estimates$term)]
}
pca_name <- paste0("PCA, ", pca_factors, " factors")
rp_pca_name <- paste0("RP-PCA, ", rp_pca_factors, " factors")
static_weights <- list(
  "1/N over all anomalies" = rep(
    1 / length(anomaly_names),
    length(anomaly_names)
  ),
  "Plug-in mean-variance" = fitted_weights(plug_in_fit),
  "Ridge (prior on Sharpe ratios)" = fitted_weights(ridge_fit),
  "Lasso on anomalies" = fitted_weights(lasso_fit),
  "Lasso on principal components" = pc_lasso_weights(
    estimation_months,
    pc_lasso_lambda
  )
)
static_weights[[pca_name]] <- factor_weights(estimation_months, pca_factors)
static_weights[[rp_pca_name]] <- factor_weights(
  estimation_months,
  rp_pca_factors,
  phi_rp
)
static_weights <- map(static_weights, as.vector)
stopifnot(!anyNA(unlist(static_weights)))

market <- read_parquet("data/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet") |>
  filter(between(date, sample_start, sample_end))

# Lecture 13: the zoo as a panel, OLS and the random forest
macro <- read_parquet("data/macro_predictors.parquet") |>
  transmute(date = date %m+% months(1), across(all_of(macro_names))) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(macro_names), \(x) {
    (x - mean(x[date < test_start])) / sd(x[date < test_start])
  }))
momentum_months <- 12
panel <- anomalies |>
  select(-y) |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "anomaly", values_to = "ret") |>
  arrange(anomaly, date) |>
  mutate(
    ret_lag_1 = lag(ret),
    momentum_12 = slider::slide_dbl(
      lag(ret),
      mean,
      .before = momentum_months - 1,
      .complete = TRUE
    ),
    .by = anomaly
  ) |>
  left_join(macro, join_by(date)) |>
  drop_na()
train <- panel |> filter(date < test_start)
features <- c("ret_lag_1", "momentum_12", macro_names)
ols_fit <- lm(reformulate(features, response = "ret"), data = train)

# Consecutive blocks of months as folds, now of the panel
block_folds <- train |>
  mutate(block = ceiling(dense_rank(date) / (n_distinct(date) / n_folds))) |>
  group_vfold_cv(group = block, v = n_folds)
forest_model <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = n_trees) |>
  set_engine("ranger", seed = 2027) |>
  set_mode("regression")
forest_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_formula(ret ~ ret_lag_1 + momentum_12 + dp + tbl + tms + dfy + svar) |>
  add_model(forest_model)
forest_tuning <- tune_grid(forest_workflow, block_folds, grid = forest_grid)
forest_fit <- forest_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(select_best(forest_tuning, metric = "rmse")) |>
  fit(train)

# Lecture 14: the predictors standardized and the return in units of its
# standard deviation, both with the estimation sample; the weight decay
# chosen on the years from validation_start; an ensemble of networks
ret_sd <- sd(train$ret)
scaled_panel <- panel |>
  mutate(
    across(all_of(features), \(x) {
      (x - mean(x[date < test_start])) / sd(x[date < test_start])
    }),
    ret_scaled = ret / ret_sd
  )
scaled_train <- filter(scaled_panel, date < test_start)
validation_start <- ymd("1995-01-01")
decay_grid <- tibble(penalty = c(1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000))
validation_split <- make_splits(
  filter(scaled_train, date < validation_start),
  assessment = filter(scaled_train, date >= validation_start)
)
validation <- manual_rset(list(validation_split), ids = "validation")
network_model <- mlp(hidden_units = 5, penalty = tune(), epochs = 500) |>
  set_engine("nnet") |>
  set_mode("regression")
network_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_variables(outcomes = ret_scaled, predictors = all_of(features)) |>
  add_model(network_model)
set.seed(1) # tune_grid() draws the random starts of the networks
network_tuning <- tune_grid(network_workflow, validation, grid = decay_grid)
best_decay <- select_best(network_tuning, metric = "rmse")
n_networks <- 5
network_forecasts <- map(seq_len(n_networks), \(seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  network_fit <- network_workflow |>
    finalize_workflow(best_decay) |>
    fit(scaled_train)
  predict(network_fit, scaled_panel)$.pred * ret_sd
})
network_forecast <- reduce(network_forecasts, `+`) / n_networks

# Lectures 13 and 14: the forecasts as expected returns, new weights every
# month with the covariance matrix and the penalty of the ridge SDF
forecasts <- list(
  "Forecasts: OLS" = predict(ols_fit, panel),
  "Forecasts: random forest" = predict(forest_fit, panel)$.pred,
  "Forecasts: neural network" = network_forecast
)
covariance <- cov(x_estimation)
forecast_weights <- map(forecasts, \(forecast) {
  panel |>
    mutate(forecast = forecast) |>
    select(date, anomaly, forecast) |>
    nest(data = -date) |>
    mutate(
      weights = map(data, \(d) {
        as.vector(solve(
          covariance + ridge_lambda * diag(length(anomaly_names)),
          d$forecast[match(anomaly_names, d$anomaly)]
        ))
      })
    ) |>
    select(date, weights)
})
```

```{r}
#| label: scoreboard-rows
#| include: false
# The anomaly returns as a matrix, one column per anomaly
returns <- as.matrix(anomalies[anomaly_names])

# Weights each month: constant for the SDF portfolios, new each month for forecasts
monthly_weights <- c(
  map(static_weights, \(w) {
    tibble(
      date = anomalies$date,
      weights = rep(list(w), nrow(anomalies))
    )
  }),
  forecast_weights
)

# Turnover between anomalies: weights scaled to a gross position of 1, and the
# weights of last month after they drifted with last month's returns
turnover <- imap(monthly_weights, \(m, portfolio) {
  rows <- match(m$date, anomalies$date)
  gross <- map(m$weights, \(w) w / sum(abs(w)))
  map_dbl(seq_along(gross)[-1], \(t) {
    drifted <- gross[[t - 1]] * (1 + returns[rows[t - 1], ])
    sum(abs(gross[[t]] - drifted / sum(abs(drifted))))
  }) |>
    tibble(date = m$date[-1], turnover = _, portfolio = portfolio)
}) |>
  bind_rows()

realized <- imap(monthly_weights, \(m, portfolio) {
  rows <- match(m$date, anomalies$date)
  tibble(
    date = m$date,
    portfolio = portfolio,
    ret = map2_dbl(m$weights, rows, \(w, r) sum(w * returns[r, ]))
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows()

cpz_runs <- read_csv(
  "lecture-slides/factor-zoo/results/cpz_light_runs.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(seeds == 9) |>
  mutate(
    model = if_else(
      str_detect(model, "Chen"),
      "Chen–Pelger–Zhu light",
      "Feed-forward SDF"
    )
  ) |>
  slice_max(sr_valid, n = 1, by = model)

scoreboard <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    portfolio = "Market",
    estimation = sharpe_ratio_vec(
      estimate = market$mkt_excess[market$date < test_start]
    ),
    test = sharpe_ratio_vec(
      estimate = market$mkt_excess[market$date >= test_start]
    )
  ),
  realized |>
    summarize(
      estimation = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = ret[date < test_start]),
      test = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = ret[date >= test_start]),
      .by = portfolio
    ),
  cpz_runs |>
    transmute(portfolio = model, estimation = sr_estimation, test = sr_test)
) |>
  left_join(
    turnover |>
      filter(date >= test_start) |>
      summarize(turnover = mean(turnover), .by = portfolio),
    join_by(portfolio)
  )

if (live) {
  ojs_define(
    poll_base = poll_base,
    scoreboard_survey = scoreboard_survey,
    ridge_test = scoreboard$test[
      scoreboard$portfolio == "Ridge (prior on Sharpe ratios)"
    ],
    test_years = test_years
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: trading-costs
#| include: false
# The zoo anomalies in the factor library: the path of each characteristic
# as in its original study (OSAP). For now the flag is in the private grid of
# the paper; the next Hugging Face release of the grid adds it
library_grid <- read_parquet(
  file.path(factor_library_paper, "data/processed/portfolio_sort_grid.parquet"),
  col_select = c("id", "sorting_variable", "is_osap_path")
)
zoo_paths <- tibble(
  anomaly = anomaly_names,
  sorting_variable = str_to_lower(anomaly_names)
) |>
  inner_join(filter(library_grid, is_osap_path), join_by(sorting_variable))

# Each month of the test sample: the turnover, the microcap share and the cost
# of each anomaly's own trades under the composite spread. The file holds the
# rows of these paths from the cost files of the paper's library build on
# UCloud (Hugging Face has the quoted spread only so far); never committed
library_costs <- read_parquet("data/factor_library_costs_zoo.parquet") |>
  inner_join(select(zoo_paths, id, anomaly), join_by(id)) |>
  filter(between(date, test_start, sample_end)) |>
  select(date, anomaly, turnover, microcap_share, cost = cost_composite_spread)
inside_turnover <- mean(library_costs$turnover)
inside_microcaps <- mean(library_costs$microcap_share, na.rm = TRUE)

# Cost per unit of turnover: what trading an anomaly's whole long and short
# legs once costs. Anomalies outside the library get the month's median
test_dates <- anomalies$date[anomalies$date >= test_start]
anomaly_costs <- expand_grid(date = test_dates, anomaly = anomaly_names) |>
  left_join(library_costs, join_by(date, anomaly)) |>
  mutate(
    cost_per_turnover = sum(cost) / sum(turnover),
    .by = anomaly
  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(c(cost, cost_per_turnover), \(x) {
      coalesce(x, median(x, na.rm = TRUE))
    }),
    .by = date
  )
cost_matrix <- function(values) {
  anomaly_costs |>
    select(date, anomaly, value = {{ values }}) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = anomaly, values_from = value) |>
    select(all_of(anomaly_names)) |>
    as.matrix()
}
inside_cost <- cost_matrix(cost)
trade_cost <- cost_matrix(cost_per_turnover)

# Each month: the return before costs, the costs of the trades inside the
# anomalies held, and the costs of the trades between anomalies, from the
# weights after last month's drift. Trades of the same stock in different
# anomalies are not netted, so the costs are an upper bound
portfolio_costs <- imap(monthly_weights, \(m, portfolio) {
  rows <- match(m$date, anomalies$date)
  map(which(m$date >= test_start), \(t) {
    month <- match(m$date[t], test_dates)
    drifted <- m$weights[[t - 1]] * (1 + returns[rows[t - 1], ])
    tibble(
      date = m$date[t],
      gross = sum(m$weights[[t]] * returns[rows[t], ]),
      inside = sum(abs(m$weights[[t]]) * inside_cost[month, ]),
      between = sum(abs(m$weights[[t]] - drifted) * trade_cost[month, ]),
      position = sum(abs(m$weights[[t]]))
    )
  }) |>
    bind_rows() |>
    mutate(portfolio = portfolio)
}) |>
  bind_rows()

after_costs <- portfolio_costs |>
  mutate(net = gross - inside - between) |>
  summarize(
    before = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = gross),
    after_inside = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = gross - inside),
    after = sharpe_ratio_vec(estimate = net),
    # Per dollar of the average gross position, per year
    mean_before = mean(gross) / mean(position) * months_per_year,
    cost_inside = mean(inside) / mean(position) * months_per_year,
    cost_between = mean(between) / mean(position) * months_per_year,
    mean_after = mean(net) / mean(position) * months_per_year,
    volatility_before = sd(gross) / mean(position) * sqrt(months_per_year),
    volatility_after = sd(net) / mean(position) * sqrt(months_per_year),
    .by = portfolio
  )
stopifnot(all.equal(
  after_costs$before,
  scoreboard$test[match(after_costs$portfolio, scoreboard$portfolio)]
))
```

## The scoreboard so far

- **Lectures 10 to 12:** the SDF, the best portfolio of the zoo, estimated directly, with shrinkage (ridge, lasso) or with a few factors (PCA, RP-PCA). The SDF weights stay constant
- **Lectures 13 and 14:** forecasts of each anomaly's return from random forests and neural networks, turned into new weights every month, and SDFs from neural networks
- Every Sharpe ratio so far is **before trading costs**, but an investor earns the return after costs

```{ojs}
//| label: class-scoreboard

class_results = surveyResults(scoreboard_survey)
class_rows = {
  if (class_results === null) return [];
  const values = id => (class_results.questions.find(q => q.id === id) || {}).values || [];
  const test = values("sharpe_test"), estimation = values("sharpe_estimation"), method = values("method");
  return test.map((t, i) => ({test: t, estimation: estimation[i], method: method[i] ?? "Other"}))
    .filter(d => d.test !== null);
}
Plot.plot({
  width: 960,
  height: 420,
  marginLeft: 230,
  x: {label: `Sharpe ratio of your SDF portfolio, ${test_years}`, grid: true},
  y: {label: null, domain: ["Ridge, lasso or elastic net", "Principal components", "Trees or random forest", "Neural network", "Other"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleX([ridge_test], {stroke: "#666666", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
    Plot.text([`Ridge SDF ${ridge_test.toFixed(2)}`], {x: ridge_test, frameAnchor: "top", dy: -6, fill: "#666666"}),
    Plot.dot(class_rows, {x: "test", y: "method", fill: "#901A1E", r: 7, fillOpacity: 0.7}),
    Plot.text([`${class_rows.length} results`], {frameAnchor: "bottom-right", dy: -6, fill: "#3d3d3d"})
  ]
})
```

# What the portfolios trade

## Turnover

```{r}
#| label: plot-turnover
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.6
turnover_shown <- c(
  "Ridge (prior on Sharpe ratios)",
  rp_pca_name,
  "Lasso on anomalies",
  "Forecasts: OLS",
  "Forecasts: random forest",
  "Forecasts: neural network"
)
scoreboard |>
  filter(portfolio %in% turnover_shown) |>
  mutate(
    portfolio = fct_reorder(portfolio, turnover),
    kind = if_else(
      str_starts(portfolio, "Forecasts"),
      "New weights every month",
      "Constant weights"
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = turnover, y = portfolio, fill = kind)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(turnover, 1)), hjust = -0.15, size = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Constant weights" = "#b3b3b3",
      "New weights every month" = ku_red
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = paste("Turnover between anomalies per month,", test_years),
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.margin = margin(5.5, 20, 5.5, 5.5))
```

- **Between anomalies:** buys plus sells as a share of the gross position. Constant SDF weights only trade back after the anomalies drift; forecasts change the weights every month
- **Inside each anomaly:** every long-short portfolio is itself rebalanced, and our returns are before these costs. In the factor library, the `r nrow(zoo_paths)` zoo anomalies built as in their original studies turn over `r percent(inside_turnover, 1)` a month and hold `r percent(inside_microcaps, 1)` of their weight in microcaps (averages `r test_years`)

# What is left after costs

## Premia before and after costs

```{r}
#| label: plot-premia
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.2
# The premium of every characteristic of the factor library, 1960–2025, in
# percent per year: built as in its original study (OSAP) or as by Jensen,
# Kelly & Pedersen (JKP), before costs and after the composite spread.
# Private paper files for now; the next Hugging Face release adds the flags
premia <- read_csv(
  file.path(factor_library_paper, "data/analysis/net_premia.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(
    window == "full",
    rule %in% c("reference", "jkp"),
    measure %in% c("gross", "composite_spread")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    construction = if_else(
      rule == "reference",
      "As in the original study (OSAP)",
      "Jensen, Kelly & Pedersen (JKP)"
    ),
    costs = if_else(measure == "gross", "Before costs", "After costs")
  )
premium_medians <- premia |>
  summarize(
    median = median(premium),
    significant = mean(t_premium > qnorm(0.975)),
    .by = c(rule, measure)
  )
microcap_median <- read_csv(
  file.path(factor_library_paper, "data/analysis/reference_path_costs.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(variable == "microcap_share") |>
  summarize(median = median(value), .by = rule) |>
  deframe()
premium_text <- function(rule_name, measure_name, statistic = "median") {
  value <- premium_medians |>
    filter(rule == rule_name, measure == measure_name) |>
    pull(statistic)
  if (statistic == "median") {
    number_text(value, 0.1, suffix = "%")
  } else {
    percent(value, 1)
  }
}
# A few premia far out in the tails stay out of the figure
premium_range <- c(-25, 25)
premia_outside <- sum(
  !between(premia$premium, premium_range[1], premium_range[2])
)
premia |>
  filter(between(premium, premium_range[1], premium_range[2])) |>
  mutate(construction = fct_rev(construction)) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = premium,
    y = construction,
    fill = fct_rev(costs),
    colour = fct_rev(costs)
  )) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = grey, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_density_ridges(
    alpha = 0.6,
    scale = 0.95,
    quantile_lines = TRUE,
    quantiles = 2,
    bandwidth = 1,
    rel_min_height = 0
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Before costs" = "#b3b3b3", "After costs" = ku_red),
    breaks = c("Before costs", "After costs")
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("Before costs" = grey, "After costs" = ku_red),
    breaks = c("Before costs", "After costs")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = percent_axis,
    limits = premium_range,
    expand = expansion(0)
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.1, 0.95))) +
  labs(
    x = "Premium of each characteristic, per year, 1960–2025",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL,
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

- `r n_distinct(premia$sorting_variable)` characteristics of the factor library (Frey, Scheuch, Voigt & Weiss), each built two ways; lines mark the medians; `r premia_outside` of `r nrow(premia)` premia lie outside. Costs: half the composite spread of every trade, the mean of four spread estimators from daily CRSP data (Chen & Velikov, 2023)
- **Medians:** as in the original studies `r premium_text("reference", "gross")` before and `r premium_text("reference", "composite_spread")` after costs; JKP `r premium_text("jkp", "gross")` and `r premium_text("jkp", "composite_spread")`. Significant before and after costs: `r premium_text("reference", "gross", "significant")` and `r premium_text("reference", "composite_spread", "significant")` (OSAP), `r premium_text("jkp", "gross", "significant")` and `r premium_text("jkp", "composite_spread", "significant")` (JKP)

::: {.highlight}
The original constructions earn the largest premia before costs and lose them to costs: the median one holds `r percent(microcap_median[["reference"]], 1)` of its weight in microcaps, against `r percent(microcap_median[["jkp"]], 1)` for JKP
:::

## The construction premium

```{r}
#| label: construction-premia-data
#| include: false
# Scheuch & Voigt (2026): the common construction premium of each choice, the
# posterior mean and standard deviation, in CAPM alpha per year relative to
# the average choice of its decision
construction_estimates <- read_parquet(
  file.path(construction_paper, "data/analysis/theta.parquet")
)
n_characteristics <- construction_estimates |>
  filter(parameter == "concept alpha") |>
  nrow()
construction_paths <- read_parquet(
  file.path(construction_paper, "data/analysis/paths.parquet"),
  col_select = "concept"
)
paths_per_characteristic <- nrow(construction_paths) / n_characteristics
common_premia <- construction_estimates |>
  filter(parameter == "common effect")
# Best minus worst path: the largest minus the smallest premium of every
# decision, summed over the decisions and rounded as in the paper
decision_ranges <- common_premia |>
  summarize(largest = max(mean_pa), smallest = min(mean_pa), .by = decision)
path_gap <- round(sum(decision_ranges$largest), 1) +
  round(-sum(decision_ranges$smallest), 1)
timing_gap <- decision_ranges |>
  filter(decision %in% c("sorting_variable_lag", "rebalancing")) |>
  summarize(gap = round(sum(largest - smallest), 1)) |>
  pull(gap)
```

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **Scheuch & Voigt (2026):** `r n_characteristics` characteristics, each built along `r comma(paths_per_characteristic)` paths of construction choices, and a Bayesian model that separates the alpha of a characteristic from the premia of its choices
- **Common construction premium:** a choice that raises the alpha of most characteristics at once, such as the choices in red
- **Best minus worst path:** `r number(path_gap, 0.1)`% per year; `r number(timing_gap, 0.1)`% from the timing (lag, rebalancing), `r number(path_gap - timing_gap, 0.1)`% from which stocks a factor holds and how
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| label: plot-construction-premia
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 5.6
#| fig-height: 4.6
# The four decisions with the largest premia, in plain names
choice_labels <- c(
  "min_size_quantile.none" = "Keep small stocks",
  "min_size_quantile.20%" = "Drop below 20th NYSE percentile",
  "sorting_variable_lag.1m" = "Lag of 1 month",
  "sorting_variable_lag.ff" = "Fama-French timing",
  "sorting_variable_lag.3m" = "Lag of 3 months",
  "sorting_variable_lag.6m" = "Lag of 6 months",
  "weighting_scheme.EW" = "Equal weights",
  "weighting_scheme.capped VW" = "Capped value weights",
  "weighting_scheme.VW" = "Value weights",
  "rebalancing.monthly" = "Rebalance monthly",
  "rebalancing.annual" = "Rebalance annually"
)
decision_labels <- c(
  min_size_quantile = "Size filter",
  sorting_variable_lag = "Lag",
  weighting_scheme = "Weights",
  rebalancing = "Rebalancing"
)
raising_choices <- c(
  "min_size_quantile.none",
  "sorting_variable_lag.1m",
  "weighting_scheme.EW",
  "rebalancing.monthly"
)
interval_quantile <- qnorm(0.975)
common_premia |>
  mutate(key = paste0(decision, ".", choice)) |>
  filter(key %in% names(choice_labels)) |>
  mutate(
    choice = factor(choice_labels[key], rev(choice_labels)),
    decision = factor(decision_labels[decision], decision_labels),
    raises = key %in% raising_choices
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_pa, y = choice, colour = raises)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = grey, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = mean_pa - interval_quantile * sd_pa,
      xend = mean_pa + interval_quantile * sd_pa
    ),
    linewidth = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_grid(decision ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = ku_red, "FALSE" = grey)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_axis) +
  labs(x = "CAPM alpha per year, with 95% interval", y = NULL) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(10, "pt")
  )
```

## The construction premium after costs

```{r}
#| label: construction-sort
#| include: false
# Scheuch & Voigt (2026), out of sample: every month, the model estimated on
# the months up to then sorts the factors of each characteristic into ten
# groups by their posterior construction premium, held over the next month.
# Returns relative to the average factor of the characteristic, CAPM alphas in
# percent per year, before costs and after half the quoted spread
construction_sort <- read_parquet(
  file.path(construction_paper, "data/analysis/construction_sort.parquet")
) |>
  filter(measure %in% c("before costs", "net 1"))
sort_months <- read_parquet(
  file.path(construction_paper, "data/analysis/construction_portfolios.parquet")
) |>
  pull(date) |>
  range()
sort_value <- function(group, measure_name, column) {
  construction_sort |>
    filter(portfolio == group, measure == measure_name) |>
    pull({{ column }})
}
break_even <- read_parquet(
  file.path(construction_paper, "data/analysis/break_even.parquet")
) |>
  filter(comparison == "construction") |>
  pull(break_even)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-construction-sort
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.3
construction_sort |>
  filter(portfolio != "high minus low") |>
  mutate(
    group = as.integer(portfolio),
    costs = if_else(
      measure == "before costs",
      "Before costs",
      "After half the quoted spread"
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = capm_alpha_pa, colour = costs)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = grey, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:10,
    labels = c("1\nSmallest", 2:9, "10\nLargest")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_axis) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Before costs" = "#b3b3b3",
      "After half the quoted spread" = ku_red
    ),
    breaks = c("Before costs", "After half the quoted spread")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Group of factors by their posterior construction premium",
    y = "CAPM alpha per year\nover the average factor",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

- **Out of sample,** `r format(sort_months[1], "%B %Y")` to `r format(sort_months[2], "%B %Y")`: the factors with the largest posterior construction premium earn a CAPM alpha of `r number(sort_value("high minus low", "before costs", capm_alpha_pa), 0.1)`% per year more than those with the smallest (t = `r number(sort_value("high minus low", "before costs", capm_t_statistic), 0.1)`), but `r number(-sort_value("high minus low", "net 1", capm_alpha_pa), 0.1)`% less after half the quoted spread of every trade (t = `r number_text(sort_value("high minus low", "net 1", capm_t_statistic), 0.1)`); the difference breaks even at `r percent(break_even, 1)` of the quoted half-spread
- **Why:** the largest group holds `r percent(sort_value("10", "before costs", microcap_share), 1)` of its weight in microcaps and turns over `r percent(sort_value("10", "before costs", turnover), 1)` a month, the smallest `r percent(sort_value("1", "before costs", microcap_share), 1)` and `r percent(sort_value("1", "before costs", turnover), 1)`

## The costs of a portfolio of anomalies

$$
r^{\text{net}}_{t} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} w_{i,t}\, r_{i,t} \;-\; \sum_{i=1}^{N} |w_{i,t}|\, c_{i,t} \;-\; \sum_{i=1}^{N} |w_{i,t} - \tilde w_{i,t}|\, \kappa_i
$$

- **Inside anomaly $i$:** $c_{i,t}$ is the cost of its own trades in month $t$, per dollar in each leg, from the factor library under the composite spread. The `r length(anomaly_names) - nrow(zoo_paths)` zoo anomalies that are not in the library get the median cost of the month
- **Between anomalies:** $\tilde w_{i,t}$ is last month's weight after it drifted with the anomaly's return. Moving one dollar into or out of anomaly $i$ costs $\kappa_i$, its average cost per unit of turnover in the library: `r number(10000 * median(trade_cost[1, ]), 1)` basis points for the median anomaly
- **An upper bound:** a stock that one anomaly buys and another sells pays twice, since we do not net trades across anomalies

## The implementable efficient frontier

```{r}
#| label: plot-frontier
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.4
# Short names in the figure
short_names <- c(
  "1/N over all anomalies" = "1/N",
  "Plug-in mean-variance" = "Plug-in",
  "Ridge (prior on Sharpe ratios)" = "Ridge",
  "Lasso on anomalies" = "Lasso",
  "Lasso on principal components" = "PC lasso",
  "Forecasts: OLS" = "OLS",
  "Forecasts: random forest" = "Random forest",
  "Forecasts: neural network" = "Neural network"
)
short_names[pca_name] <- "PCA"
short_names[rp_pca_name] <- "RP-PCA"
market_sharpe <- scoreboard$test[scoreboard$portfolio == "Market"]
after_costs |>
  mutate(
    name = short_names[portfolio],
    kind = if_else(
      str_starts(portfolio, "Forecasts"),
      "Forecasts: new weights every month",
      "SDFs: constant weights"
    ),
    kind = fct_rev(kind)
  ) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = grey, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = market_sharpe,
    intercept = 0,
    colour = grey,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  # Arrows end just before the points after costs
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = 100 * volatility_before,
      y = 100 * mean_before,
      xend = 100 *
        (volatility_before + 0.95 * (volatility_after - volatility_before)),
      yend = 100 * (mean_before + 0.95 * (mean_after - mean_before))
    ),
    colour = "#b3b3b3",
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.1, "inches"), type = "closed")
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(x = 100 * volatility_before, y = 100 * mean_before),
    colour = grey,
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(x = 100 * volatility_after, y = 100 * mean_after),
    colour = ku_red,
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(x = 100 * volatility_before, y = 100 * mean_before, label = name),
    colour = jet,
    bg.colour = "white",
    bg.r = 0.2,
    size = 3.8,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    point.padding = 0.3,
    min.segment.length = 0.2,
    segment.colour = grey,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    seed = 1
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = percent_axis,
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_axis) +
  facet_wrap(~kind, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = paste("Volatility per year,", test_years),
    y = "Mean return per year"
  ) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(20, "pt")
  )
```

- **Grey before, red after costs,** per dollar of the average gross position: the slope of a line from the origin is a Sharpe ratio (dashed: the market, `r number(market_sharpe, 0.01)`)
- **Jensen, Kelly, Malamud & Pedersen (2026):** the *implementable efficient frontier*, the best return after costs at each level of risk. Weights learned with the costs in the objective beat forecasts that ignore them

::: {.highlight}
Before costs a free lunch; after the costs inside the anomalies none earns a premium. The costs belong in the objective
:::

## Scoreboard of the machine learning lectures

```{r}
#| label: scoreboard-table
#| echo: false
# After costs: the mean return per year per dollar of the average gross
# position, since the Sharpe ratio of a negative mean says nothing (more
# volatility would raise it). The market pays no costs here
market_mean <- mean(market$mkt_excess[market$date >= test_start]) *
  months_per_year
scoreboard |>
  left_join(select(after_costs, portfolio, mean_after), join_by(portfolio)) |>
  mutate(
    mean_after = if_else(portfolio == "Market", market_mean, mean_after),
    across(c(estimation, test), \(x) number(x, 0.01)),
    turnover = if_else(is.na(turnover), "–", percent(turnover, 1)),
    mean_after = if_else(is.na(mean_after), "–", percent_text(mean_after, 0.1))
  ) |>
  select(
    Portfolio = portfolio,
    `Sharpe ratio, estimation` = estimation,
    "Sharpe ratio {test_years}" := test,
    `Turnover between anomalies` = turnover,
    `After costs` = mean_after
  )
```

- **After costs:** the mean return per year `r test_years` per dollar of the gross position, after the costs of the last slides; the market pays none. –: no anomalies (market) or no stored weights (network SDFs)
- The trading game charges 10 bps of every trade since 1 March: your own record is a row of this scoreboard

## Backup: where the costs come from

```{r}
#| label: backup-costs-table
#| echo: false
after_costs |>
  mutate(
    across(c(mean_before, cost_inside, cost_between, mean_after), \(x) {
      percent_text(x, 0.1)
    })
  ) |>
  select(
    Portfolio = portfolio,
    "Before costs" = mean_before,
    "Costs inside the anomalies" = cost_inside,
    "Costs between anomalies" = cost_between,
    "After costs" = mean_after
  )
```

Mean returns and costs per year, `r test_years`, per dollar of the average gross position. Constant SDF weights pay almost only the costs inside the anomalies; the forecasts also pay for their trades between anomalies
